No, not all of it. Of the roughly 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss mapped in 2021, the MGAP 2021 forest map places about 68.1 ha (around 84%) in planted forest, specifically Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda. The other 13.2 ha (about 16%) falls outside any mapped forest, and none of it is in native forest.

Two caveats:
- A further 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event, so it isn't covered by this breakdown.
- The planted-forest label is territorial context only. It doesn't show the cause of the loss (harvest, fire, storm or clearing). It also doesn't show whether deforestation or land-use change occurred, or whether the loss was legal or compliant.
